title: Got tired of manually executing Telegram signals, so I built this
author: Glittering_Pass8656
selftext:
I'm in the Thomas Kralow trading community and I was getting annoyed with manually executing every signal.

Telegram notification comes in.

Open exchange.

Copy entry.

Calculate risk.

Calculate position size.

Add SL.

Add TP1, TP2, TP3, TP4, TP5...

And if you're not fast enough, the entry can already be gone.

I'm a developer, so naturally I ended up building something for it 😅

It's called **SignalToOrder**.

It reads the Telegram signal, with help of AI understands the setup, calculates the trade based on your risk settings and sends the order to EVEDEX automatically.

I'm still developing/testing it, so I'm not really trying to sell anything here.

I'm mainly interested in knowing whether other people trading signals have the same problem.

If anyone wants to test it, I'm probably going to give access to a very small number of people first.

Don't get me wrong I am not affiliated with Thomas Kralow or EVEDEX. Also, the tool doesn't provide or redistribute signals, it only automates signals the user already receives.

[https://signaltoorder.app/](https://signaltoorder.app/)

Would love to hear what you guys think.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the parsing is where this bites. signal groups edit messages after posting, send "TP1 hit, move SL to entry" as a follow-up, and now and then typo an entry by a digit. I'd put a dumb check after the AI step that refuses any order where the stop is on the wrong side of entry or the size is over your cap, no matter what the model understood.

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Thanks, appreciate the feedback! We use AI to extract and format the signal into structured JSON with a strict schema. It’s been very effective with the channel’s message format, and we cross-check the extracted values against a rule-based parser.

Valid JSON is only the first step. Before submitting an entry, the backend checks the setup against current EVEDEX market, account and instrument data. That includes checking the SL/TP levels, calculating position size from the configured risk, and enforcing position and margin limits. The AI can’t override those checks.

Once the entry is filled, position management is handled entirely by the backend using predefined rules and confirmed exchange data. SL/TP management and break-even don’t depend on further AI decisions or blindly following a “TP1 hit” message.

You’re right that a plausible typo could still pass extraction, though, and later edits/corrections aren’t something I’d claim is fully solved. That’s why the independent backend checks matter.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the market-data check before entry is the good part. the one I'd add is staleness: if the message is a few minutes old, or price already ran through the entry, skip it rather than chase.

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Yes yes, I’ve already implemented this checker. Different channels have different expiry windows depending on the trading style. Scalping signals have a shorter window, while swing setups remain valid longer, measured from the original Telegram message timestamp.

Before submitting an entry, Autopilot checks the live price again. Expired signals are skipped, and automatic entries only happen within the signal’s entry range.s

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: anchoring on the original message timestamp is the right call. I'd watch edits though, an edited message shouldn't reset that clock.

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Hmm, you have a good point here.  
 In the Telegram channels that I'm currently using, messages are not edited at all. But for future safety, I could definitely add checks for edited or updated messages before allowing any execution.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: makes sense if your channels never edit. cheap to add anyway, the first one that does will be the day it matters.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good luck with it, curious how the edit handling goes.

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Yes totally agree , win rate alone doesn’t show profitability. You can win 8 trades at $10 each and lose 2 at $50 each, and still be down $20 before fees. Average win/loss size, position sizing and trading costs all matter.

I shared the numbers to be transparent about my actual results, not as proof that the signals are profitable. That’s also why I mentioned being down $300 at the time.

comments.author: amazinZero
comments.body:
I have quite the same thing, but it creates several legs for every trade every TP. While one is closed on TP1, 2nd leg waits for TP2 to hit etc. Some BE logic also build around this. 

Reg your build, I’m not sure I will ever trust any kind of service my telegram account. To read messages in “signal groups” user must provide the access to the account. This will never happen (if the account is personal). It’s good if it’s open source with possibility to run on your own vps.

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Your multileg approach sounds useful! Mine also handles multiple TPs and break-even based on confirmed exchange fills, after that TP1 has hit.

The Telegram access concern is completely logical. But reading private channels requires an authenticated session, and a “read-only” application doesn’t mean the session itself has restricted permissions.

I originally built this for my own use. For other users, a self-hosted reader that keeps the Telegram session on their own machine or VPS makes a lot of sense. That’s a deployment option worth exploring, rather than expecting everyone to trust a service with their personal account. Appreciate you raising it!

replies.author: Glittering_Pass8656
replies.body:
Haha, fair point, you are right 50%.  
I use LLMs heavily because they help me move much faster, but I wouldn’t call it 100% vibe coding. The architecture, debugging, product logic and final decisions are still on me.

I see it more as AI-assisted development, AI writes a lot of code, but I still need to understand it, review it and own the result.
